$\begin{align}
y^2\,dy&=2x\,dx
\\\\
\displaystyle\int y^2\,dy&=\displaystyle\int 2x\,dx
\\\\
\dfrac{y^3}{3}&=x^2+C_1
\\\\
y^3&=3x^2+C
\\\\
y&=\sqrt[3]{3x^2+C}
\end{align}$

[[☃ explanation 1]]

Notice that after the integration, more work was required in order to isolate $y$.

options.explanation: Since ${3C_1}$ is still some arbitrary constant, we just called it $C$.

hints.content:
In conclusion, this is the solution of the equation:

$y=\sqrt[3]{3x^2+C}$
